---
title: "Evaluation under an alternative posterior law"
subtitle: "2.17 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 16 and 18"
description: "Fixed-report risk and regret under distinct selection and evaluation laws."
---

An analyst can select a report under one posterior law and evaluate it under another. We hold the selected report fixed while changing one site's evaluation mean or all of the evaluation standard deviations. For each change, we compute the risk of the same report under both laws. We then compare its evaluation risk with the lowest risk attainable under the evaluation law in the same report family. The difference from that minimum is evaluation regret.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Same laws.** The selected report has risk .0417 under either law, and evaluation regret is 0. The plotted
  intervals and means coincide; the largest pair-error gap is also 0. Changing the evaluation law shows how far the two assessments can diverge.
- **Move C upward.** The frozen report's evaluation risk rises to .1360, while the evaluation-best report has
  risk .0542. Their difference, .0817, is the regret. The chosen reports change 3 pair decisions. The table separates the two evaluations of each report.
- **Wider evaluation law.** The frozen report now has risk .0779, yet regret remains 0. It is still best in the
  family under the evaluation law. A change in the risk of a report does not by itself imply that another
  report should replace it.
- **C +.40, no cap.** Evaluation regret is .0108. Both optimizations now search the larger family. The family labels identify the same set of eligible reports for both calculations.
- **Small change, new report.** There is 1 changed pair decision. **How the bounds are calculated** gives the pair-error radius of .0132. Regret is
  only .0008, beneath the uniform bound .0263. A small objective gap can coexist with different grade vectors.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Both laws use independent normal distributions specified for the example. The regret bound adds two quantities: twice a uniform bound on the difference in risks across laws and a bound on the selection-law optimization gap. Both bounds apply to the whole common family. We enumerate every report, so the selection-law optimization gap is zero. Increasing the number of draws under either law would leave any difference between the two laws in place.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
g <- c(A=1L,B=1L,C=2L,D=2L,E=3L,F=3L)
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_tutorial$one, weights=c(score_A=1), tau=.2)$weighted_risk # .04165164
```
:::

Standalone: [two evaluation laws](../../embed/another-law.html), for example `?shift=1&unit=C`.

Related applications: [Reporting risk and withholding cost](price-of-silence.qmd),
